question: Three points $A(1,0,2)$, $B(3,2,-1)$ and $C(-1,4,1)$ define a triangular path. A mathematical model represents each movement by a directed vector. Students first calculate the vectors along two consecutive sides and compare their sum with the direct vector from $A$ to $C$. They then include the return vector from $C$ to $A$ to examine the resultant of the complete closed path.(a) Determine $\overrightarrow{AB}$.(b) Calculate $\overrightarrow{BC}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$.(c) Verify the relation $\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}=\overrightarrow{AC}$.(d) Obtain $\overrightarrow{CA}$ and show that the resultant vector for the closed path is a zero vector.
explanation: (a)`\overrightarrow{AB}=(3-1)\hat{i}+(2-0)\hat{j}+(-1-2)\hat{k}\overrightarrow{AB}=2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-3\hat{k}`(b)`\overrightarrow{BC}=(-1-3)\hat{i}+(4-2)\hat{j}+[1-(-1)]\hat{k}\overrightarrow{BC}=-4\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}`Also,`\overrightarrow{AC}=(-1-1)\hat{i}+(4-0)\hat{j}+(1-2)\hat{k}\overrightarrow{AC}=-2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-\hat{k}`(c)`\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}=(2-4)\hat{i}+(2+2)\hat{j}+(-3+2)\hat{k}\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}=-2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-\hat{k}`Therefore,`\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}=\overrightarrow{AC}`(d)`\overrightarrow{CA}=(1+1)\hat{i}+(0-4)\hat{j}+(2-1)\hat{k}\overrightarrow{CA}=2\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+\hat{k}=-\overrightarrow{AC}`Thus,`\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}+\overrightarrow{CA}=\overrightarrow{AC}+\overrightarrow{CA}=\vec{0}`Hence, the resultant vector for the closed path is the zero vector.
